name: NextQA
intro: NExT-QA 是面向解释性视频问答的人工标注基准，从 6,000 个 VidOR 视频中保留 5,440 个交互丰富片段并构建 52,044 条因果、时序和描述性问答。论文提供 47,692 道五选一题与完整开放式任务；两条分支分别使用精确选项准确率和开放式 WUPS，未定义跨任务合并分数。
build_method: VidOR 视频筛选, 分阶段双角色人工标注, 困难干扰项生成
metric: 五选一选项准确率, 开放式 WUPS@0（二元与计数题精确匹配）
task_type: 视频问答, 因果推理, 时序推理
eval_feature: 因果/时序/描述问题, 多选与开放式问答, 人工标注
task_type_en: Video QA, Causal Reasoning, Temporal Reasoning
build_method_en: VidOR Video Selection, Staged Dual-role Human Annotation, Hard Distractor Generation
eval_feature_en: Causal, Temporal, and Descriptive Questions; Multi-choice and Open-ended QA; Human Annotation
intro_en: NExT-QA is a manually annotated explanatory-video-QA benchmark. It retains 5,440 interaction-rich clips from 6,000 VidOR videos and contains 52,044 causal, temporal, and descriptive QA pairs. The paper provides 47,692 five-option items and the full open-ended task; the branches use exact option accuracy and open-ended WUPS respectively, with no cross-task aggregate defined.
metric_en: Five-option Accuracy; Open-ended WUPS@0 with Exact Match for Binary and Counting

drawio_review_note: Paper/source audit fixed on 2026-07-18. The primary paper is arXiv:2105.08276v2; the reviewed PDF has SHA-256 c2c9514af844bbd8a44117d8ffa1e91106e4c4b6d58911766e77725186b31670. Sections 3.1-4 and Appendix A were checked against the diagram. Released multiple-choice semantics were checked at official doc-doc/NExT-QA commit 2432e9724f88ed9f40010e2989f104570a91de4e, and open-ended semantics at official doc-doc/NExT-OE commit a83f8f581191da07675e0fc83074e0dfcf907273. The paper begins with 6,000 VidOR videos originally drawn from YFCC-100M, selecting clips that are longer and rich in objects and interactions without restricting actors or activities. Videos are randomly split 7:1:2 before question annotation. One hundred trained undergraduates work under supervision for one year in three stages: causal questions first, temporal questions second, and descriptive questions last. The protocol uses a question-type drop-down, suggests maximum lengths of 22 words per question and six words per answer, and lets questioners report videos on which effective questions cannot be written. Question and answer roles are separated. Answerers first check question quality, repair a bad question when possible, delete unusable questions, and require answers to be objective and visibly inferable from the video. Post-processing removes confirmed boring videos, deletes some yes-answered validation/test items to balance yes/no answers, and removes counting questions whose answers exceed twenty. The resulting open-ended corpus has 5,440 videos and 52,044 QA pairs, split into 3,870/570/1,000 videos; causal, temporal, and descriptive questions account for 48%, 29%, and 23%. Multiple-choice generation excludes binary questions, groups the remainder by annotated type, retrieves the top 50 similar questions using Sentence-BERT question embeddings, and treats their answers as distractor candidates. Candidate answers are removed when lemmatized forms match after stop-word removal or answer-vector similarity exceeds 0.9; candidates below 0.2 similarity to the correct answer are also discarded so retained negatives remain hard. Four candidates are sampled, the correct answer is inserted evenly among five positions, and every tuple is manually checked and amended. This produces 47,692 five-option items. The released multiple-choice scorer compares answer and prediction indices exactly and reports fine-grained types, causal/temporal/descriptive aggregates, and overall accuracy; the paper's 88.38% human result is a multiple-choice validation reference, not an open-ended human score. The separate NExT-OE scorer lemmatizes text after custom stop-word removal, applies exact equality to binary and counting questions, applies WUPS with alpha 0 otherwise, and takes the better score when an additional reference answer exists. The paper reports multiple-choice accuracy and open-ended WUPS separately and defines no combined score across the two tasks. Both repositories use MIT licenses; QA annotations and scorers are public, while raw videos are distributed through linked Drive resources. The exact original annotation logs, random split seed, Sentence-BERT construction program, and full manual amendment history are not released, so the diagram shows those reproducibility boundaries rather than implying end-to-end reconstruction from code. Formal publication evidence [site-a11x-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 3592×561 (English) and 3583×561 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 3590×559 and 3581×559. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
